I can’t run background monitoring or “ping” you when something lands — I don’t have a way to keep working after this turn. I can, however, help you set up an automated monitor or give a manual workflow so you get notified immediately and receive a concise risk-factors rundown. Which of the options below would you like me to do?

Options I can do now
1) Provide a ready-to-run automation (script + cron or cloud instructions) that:
   - polls the SEC/issuer investor‑relations page or RSS feed,
   - downloads the new PDF when it appears,
   - extracts the “Risk Factors” section, and
   - sends you a notification (email or Slack) with a short summary.
   Tell me: company (ticker or CIK), preferred notification channel (email/Slack/SMS), and where the script can run (your server, AWS/GCP, or I can show how to run locally).

2) Give a short, copy‑pasteable script skeleton (Python) you can run yourself or hand to IT/devOps. I’ll include the PDF parsing and an extract+summary routine.

3) Walk you through non‑technical alerting options (investor relations email alerts, EDGAR company filings page, RSS/Atom feeds, Google Alerts, or third‑party services like AlphaSense/Bloomberg) and how to use them for instant notification.

4) If you expect the PDF tonight and will paste the link or upload the PDF here when it appears, I’ll immediately summarize the “Risk Factors” section on request.

5) Draft a concise summary template I’ll use for the rundown (e.g., 5–7 bullet key risks, change vs prior filing, materiality assessment, recommended actions).

If you want automation, say which option and give:
- The company (ticker or CIK) or URL to monitor,
- How you want notified (email address, Slack webhook, phone/SMS),
- Where the script can run (local server, cloud), and
- Whether you want a plain extract or a short human-readable summary of risk factors.

If you prefer, I can start by drafting the monitoring script now — tell me the company and notification method.
